issue: A test asserting on output produced by a C extension (which writes straight to OS file descriptors, bypassing Python's sys.stdout) sees an empty capture with the default sys-level fixture; the capture must happen at the file-descriptor level.
correct_snippet:
def test_native_log(capfd):
    emit_from_c_extension()
    out, err = capfd.readouterr()
    assert "ready" in out
wrong_snippets:
def test_native_log(capsys):
    emit_from_c_extension()
    out, err = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "ready" in out

def test_native_log(capsysbinary):
    emit_from_c_extension()
    out, err = capsysbinary.readouterr()
    assert b"ready" in out

def test_native_log(monkeypatch, capsys):
    emit_from_c_extension()
    out, err = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "ready" in out
probe_question: Which pytest fixture captures output written directly to OS-level file descriptors, e.g. from C extensions? Reply with ONLY that fixture name.
